newsitem.title: DENMARK: Protesters occupy Peru's consulate in Copenhagen.
newsitem.headline: Protesters occupy Peru's consulate in Copenhagen.

text.p: Danish police said on Monday that Peru's consulate-general in Copenhagen had been occupied by a handful of young Danish demonstrators.

"We have no clear picture of the situation at the moment but it seems that some young people are hanging out of the building's window and shouting slogans," a police spokesman told the Danish Ritzau news agency.

The agency quoted a spokesman for the Danish branch of the so-called Committee for the Release of MRTA Prisoners in Peru as saying the action was in sympathy with the 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels who died in last week's storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
Police cordoned off the area round the consulate in eastern Copenhagen and said there were four or five Danish activists involved in the occupation.

Ritzau said the protesters issued a statement calling for an immediate inquiry into the Peruvian army's action in ending the five-month hostage drama in Lima last week and demanding that the Danish government condemn it.
All but one of 72 hostages held in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima by MRTA fighters were rescued alive in last week's raid.
One Peruvian hostage and two soldiers died along with all 14 MRTA rebels. Peruvian radio reported at the weekend that a third commando had died, but this was denied by a hospital official.
